root_idea.summary: The root denotes overcoming joined with superiority or elevation over another, extending to subduing, humbling, and being placed under domination.
root_idea.development: Its lexical development includes active conquest and subjugation, abasement and coercion, passive subjection, and a specialized usage for flesh affected by fire until its juices flow. The root discussion also records more remote or exceptional extensions involving a hard stone, a he-goat, and moving backward; these are not direct Quranic meanings.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form.
Displayed as the singular active-participial citation form.
Displayed as the intensive adjective or active-participial form.

senses.definition: To oppress or humiliate by subduing or overbearing someone.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence, it is a prohibition against oppressing or humiliating the orphan.

senses.definition: One who overcomes, conquers, or subdues.
senses.usage_conditions: This is the agentive use, including the plural description of people who exercise subjugating power.

senses.definition: The Subduer of created beings by sovereign authority and power.
senses.usage_conditions: As a divine epithet, it includes disposing of creatures as desired, with or against their will.

senses.definition: Intensively one who overcomes and subdues—the Irresistible.
senses.usage_conditions: A divine adjective emphasizing overwhelming or pervasive subduing power; all Quranic occurrences are in divine descriptions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To overcome, conquer, subdue, overpower, master, prevail over, or abase.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The comparative أَقْهَرُ expresses a greater or greatest degree of subduing or abasing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To force, compel, or coerce someone, including taking someone by force against their will.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: قَهَرَهُ عَلَى الأَمْرِ expresses compelling someone to do something; قَهْرًا can describe forcible taking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of flesh: to become affected by fire so that its juice flows.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized culinary usage describing flesh acted upon by heat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become overcome, conquered, subdued, or abased; transitively, to find or cause someone to be in a subdued state.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The causative use can mean placing someone under the power of one who overcomes him.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be overcome, subdued, or overpowered.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A quasi-passive derived use related to قَهَرَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An imprecation wishing that a person or group be overcome and subdued.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed formula of invocation or imprecation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person liable to be overcome, conquered, or subdued by everyone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the construction فُلَانٌ قُهْرَةٌ لِلنَّاسِ.
An adverbial use describing an action performed under compulsion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman characterized by evil, injustice, or corruptness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a distinct lexical noun, not a general restriction on the root's other meanings.
A figurative usage applied to mountains.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Abasing is included in the broader overcoming branch.
Coercion is grouped with the compulsion branch.
Form IV state of being overcome.
The abased state is covered by the Form IV entry.
Transitive finding or placing someone in subjection.
Distinct lexical noun for a corrupt woman.
Comparative degree is covered under the overcoming branch.

cautions: The Quranic Form I occurrence is normalized from the imperfect form تَقْهَرْ to the classical citation form قَهَرَ.
The QAC nominal tag for قَاهِر occurrences is presented as an active participle because the supplied derived morphology identifies them as ACTIVE_PARTICIPLE.
